title: Smallest Subarrays With Maximum Bitwise OR
summary: Given an array nums of non-negative integers, for each index i, determine the smallest subarray starting at i that has the maximum possible bitwise OR.
statement: Given an array nums of non-negative integers, for each index i, determine the smallest subarray starting at i that has the maximum possible bitwise OR. The result is an array where each element represents the length of the minimum sized subarray starting at the corresponding index with the maximum bitwise OR.
constraints: For every index i, consider nonempty subarrays beginning at i.
Find the maximum bitwise OR any such subarray can obtain.
Return the shortest length attaining that maximum for each starting index.
hints: Scan starts from right to left while recording the nearest position at or after i containing each bit.
Update a bit’s last position when nums[i] contains it.
The subarray must extend through the farthest recorded required-bit position.
The suffix maximum OR contains exactly the bits with recorded positions, and reaching their farthest first occurrence is both necessary and sufficient.
editorial: The suffix maximum OR contains exactly the bits with recorded positions, and reaching their farthest first occurrence is both necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: From index 0 the maximum OR 3 first appears at length 3; repeating this gives [3,3,2,2,1].
Every subarray has OR zero, so length one is already sufficient at both indexes.
